answer: Random 9-juror sampling at the inlet: each identity admitted via the mesa of staked work, then graders drawn without replacement per case. A farm holding k% of identities captures a full jury only k^9 of the time. At k=0.3 that's 0.002% per verdict, so expected extraction collapses below attack cost. Honest jurors dominate the zenith of vote weight, and sybils bleed stake before swinging one ruling. Verdicts stay uncapturable because quadratic jury probability beats linear identity accumulation.
